text: A few mistakes trip up beginners here. Mixing up program and programming — treating them as the same word. One is the process; one is the finished set of instructions. Imagining the computer can reason or guess what you meant. It can't — it only does what it is told. Thinking programming is just typing code or memorising a language. The real work is turning a problem into ordered steps; the language is only how you write them down. Assuming the order of instructions does not matter. It always does.
